properties.snippet: Tennessee water quality assessment results for the 2026 cycle, including polygon and polyline water resources and a supporting table of potential pollution sources. The service tracks attainment status, assessment rationale, and watershed context for statewide reporting.
properties.description:
Overview

This feature service compiles Tennessee water quality assessment results for the 2026 cycle. It supports statewide tracking of assessed water resources and their status relative to water quality standards, including waters identified as impaired or threatened due to pollution concerns.  The 2026 assessment includes updates for Group 1 and 2 watersheds within the Division of Water Resources watershed planning process.  These feature layers are intended to provide the spatial visualization of the Tennessee 2026 List of Impaired and Threatened Steams.  The Tennessee 2026 List of Impaired and Threatened Streams is the official EPA approved document for water quality impairment.

Feature Layers

  • Water Quality Assessment Streams (2026) — Polyline features representing assessed linear water resources such as streams or river segments. Records include assessment unit name, location description, water type, length, attainment status, watershed context, and rationale for the assessment decision.
  • Water Quality Assessment Waterbodies (2026) — Polygon features representing assessed water bodies and water resource areas. Records include assessment unit name, location description, water type, size, attainment status, watershed context, and rationale for the assessment decision.
  • Water Quality Assessment Potential Sources (2026) — Supporting table listing assessment units with associated rationale, parameter codes, source types for potential pollution sources linked to water quality assessment findings.

Geographic Coverage

The service covers Tennessee and supports statewide water quality assessment and reporting.

Use Cases

  • Reviewing water quality attainment status for individual water bodies and stream segments
  • Supporting Tennessee water quality planning and Section 303(d) reporting
  • Identifying assessment units associated with parameters (causes) of pollution
  • Providing public access to compiled water quality assessment results

properties.snippet: Official boundaries for all State Forests managed by the Tennessee Division of Forestry (TDF). This is the authoritative dataset for TDF-managed forest lands.
properties.description:
Tennessee State Forest Boundaries

Overview

This feature layer represents the official and authoritative boundaries of all State Forests administered by the Tennessee Division of Forestry (TDF). The polygons in this dataset delineate the properties managed by the TDF for sustainable forestry, wildlife habitat, soil and water conservation, and public recreation.

This dataset is intended for use in planning, management, analysis, and public information purposes. It serves as the primary GIS data source for all TDF-managed forest properties.

Feature Layer

  • Tennessee State Forest Boundaries: This polygon layer represents the official boundaries of all State Forests administered by the Tennessee Division of Forestry. 

Data Attributes

  • StateForestName: The common name of the State Forest.
  • AbbrCode: The abbreviated codes.
  • County: The county(ies) that the State Forest is located in.
  • District: The TDF Administrative District that the State Forest is located in.
  • Acres: The calculated acreage of the property.
  • Latitude: Latitude of the center point of the property, in Decimal Degrees.
  • Longitude: Longitude of the center point of the property, in Decimal Degrees.
  • YearEst: The year that the State Forest was established.
  • Notes: Additional notes.
  • CollectionMethod: The method of boundary delineation.
  • Hyperlink: The hyperlink to the State Forests' webpage.

Data Maintenance

This layer is actively maintained by the TDF Forest Data and Analysis Unit. It is updated periodically to reflect new acquisitions, boundary surveys, and other administrative changes.
properties.licenseInfo:
Credits

Tennessee Division of Forestry - Forest Data and Analysis Unit

Access and Use Constraints

This dataset is intended for planning, management, analysis, and public information purposes. While the Tennessee Division of Forestry strives for a high degree of accuracy, this data is not a substitute for an official, on-the-ground legal survey. The information is provided “as is” without warranty or guarantee of any kind as to its accuracy, content, completeness, legality, or reliability. For all legal property boundary questions or transactions, please refer to the official deeds and surveys on file.

properties.snippet: Tennessee soil units derived from gSSURGO dataset published by the USDA. This is a TDF authoritative dataset for statewide soils.
properties.description:
Overview

This feature layer represents the authoritative statewide soil units derived from the U.S. Department of Agriculture's (USDA) Gridded Soil Survery Geopgraphic database (gSSURGO). The polygons in this dataset delineate the boundaries of soil units for use in assisting sustainable forestry, wildlife habitat, soil and water conservation, and public recreation.

This dataset is intended for use in planning, management, analysis, and public information purposes. It serves as the primary TDF GIS data source for Tennessee soils.

Data Attributes

  • AREASYMBOL: The state area symbol of the mapunit.
  • SPATIALVER: The spatial version of the mapunit.
  • MUSYM: The abbreviated symbol of the soil mapunit.
  • MUKEY: The mapunit key field is found throughout SSURGO and provides a primary link between the geographic and tabular data.
  • MUNAME: The full mapunit name.
  • FARM: The farmland classification of the mapunit.
  • ACRES: Acreage of the mapunit.
  • HYDRICRATING: The hydric rating of the mapunit.
  • LCPRIMARY: The primary land cover classification of the mapunit.
  • LCSECONDARY: The secondary land cover classification of the mapunit.
  • DRAINAGECLASS: The drainage class of the mapunit.
  • HYDROGROUP: The soil hydrologic group code of the mapunit.
  • FROSTFREEDAYS: Number of frost free days in a calendar year, on average, of the mapunit.
  • SOILORDER: The taxonomic soil order of the mapunit.

Data Maintenance

This layer is actively maintained by the TDF Forest Data and Analysis Unit. It is updated periodically to reflect new data publishes from the gSSURGO dataset.

properties.snippet: This service maps Tennessee's paddling access sites, detailing facilities, amenities, and access information for statewide recreational water use.
properties.description:
Overview

This feature service provides comprehensive spatial data paddling access locations across the state of Tennessee. It is designed to support recreational water activities and public access planning by detailing key site features and amenities.

Feature Layers

  • Paddling Access Sites: This layer catalogs numerous paddling access sites throughout Tennessee. It includes detailed attributes such as county, waterway, parking types and capacities, hours of operation, and available amenities like ice, bait, camping, and restrooms. The dataset also characterizes ramp structures, number of lanes, trailer parking, and access restrictions such as trolling or motorized vessel allowances. Ownership and management information is provided to clarify jurisdictional responsibilities. This layer is essential for users needing precise information on public boating facilities, their accessibility, and available services.

Geographic Coverage

The data covers a wide geographic area restricted to the state of Tennessee, including comprehensive listing of counties served. The dataset is suitable for statewide boating and fishing access planning, resource management, and recreational use analysis.

Use Cases

  • Supporting recreational boating, fishing, and paddling activities by providing detailed access site information.
  • Assisting governmental and resource agencies in managing boat ramps, marinas, and public water access points.
  • Informing the public and stakeholders about locations, facilities, and services available at each site.
  • Enabling spatial analyses related to waterway accessibility, facility distribution, and regional outdoor recreation planning.

properties.snippet: This service maps trout stocking locations throughout Tennessee, detailing stocking programs, species, access, and management authorities for statewide fisheries support.
properties.description:
Overview

This feature service provides detailed geographic information about trout stocking locations managed by various entities within the state of Tennessee. It is intended to serve anglers, wildlife managers, and conservationists interested in trout fisheries.

Feature Layer
  • Trout_MASTER_Project: This layer contains point features representing trout stocking sites including streams, ponds, and reservoirs across Tennessee. The data includes precise geographic coordinates and site-specific details such as site name, stream name, region, county, and city.

Each site records key attributes such as the stocking program season (e.g., Spring, Winter), water type (stream, pond, reservoir), and species stocked (Rainbow, Brook, Brown, or combinations thereof). Additional management information is provided, including ownership or management authority (e.g., Private Land, USFS, TVA), access information such as 24-hour availability, sunrise/sunset accessibility, and parking facilities.

Geographic Coverage

The dataset covers multiple regions throughout Tennessee, including various counties and municipalities, providing comprehensive statewide coverage for trout stocking efforts.

Potential Applications
  • Supporting recreational fishing by identifying stocked trout locations and access details.
  • Assisting wildlife and fisheries management in monitoring and planning stocking activities.
  • Enabling environmental and conservation research related to freshwater ecosystems in Tennessee.

properties.snippet: This service features detailed data on Tennessee marinas, including amenities, parking, and access information for statewide recreational use.
properties.description:
Overview

This feature service provides comprehensive data on marinas located throughout the state of Tennessee. It is designed to support recreational boating and fishing activities by offering detailed information about facilities and amenities available across various public access points to waterways.

Feature Layer: Marina Sites

This primary layer represents individual marina locations. It includes detailed attributes such as geographic coordinates, county, associated waterway, and site name. The layer categorizes sites with descriptors for parking availability and surface type, hours of operation, and access fees, enhancing usability for public and agency personnel.

Key features covered include:

  • Location and type of access sites such as boat launches, marinas, and fishing sites.
  • Parking details including surface type and capacity, including trailer parking.
  • Facilities and amenities like gas availability, ice, bait, camping, restrooms, fishing piers, fish cleaning stations, and courtesy docks.
  • Operational considerations such as access hours, seasonal closures, and 24-hour availability.
  • Site ownership and management information by various government and private entities.
  • Accessibility features including handicap and lighted parking.
  • Restrictions or special conditions such as trolling-only areas or rental availability.

Geographic Coverage

The dataset covers the entire state of Tennessee, with sites organized by county and waterway, providing statewide access to boating facilities.

Use Cases

  • Planning and management of recreational boating and fishing infrastructure by state and local agencies.
  • Providing the public with detailed site information for trip planning and safe boating access.
  • Supporting emergency response and maintenance scheduling for water access points.
